title: Verifier-integrated LLM intent→configuration pipeline: an artifact-grounded paired evaluation and lessons from a ceiling effect
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired experiment (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) studying whether integrating an automated network verifier (block-on-violation) into an LLM intent→configuration pipeline reduces unsafe enactments. Using gpt-5-mini and a shared-initial-candidate generation policy across 150 paired intents (300 episodes), we compared LLM-only (baseline) and LLM+verifier-block (guarded). All 150 generated candidates were accepted by the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) under both pipelines (n11=150, n10=n01=n00=0). The preregistered McNemar comparison is uninformative (p=1.0); paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). We report complete, artifact-backed execution and scoring traces (representative files and SHA256 listed inline), diagnose why a ceiling effect occurred (identical shared-initial outputs and acceptance predicates), correct a preregistration/execution mismatch (the preregistered rollback hypothesis H2 was not testable/executed), and give artifact-grounded recommendations (adversarial/stateful task banks; multi-model/multi-verifier matrices) to expose verifier-sensitive failure modes. All raw transcripts, validator traces, scoring JSONs, analysis scripts, and SHA256 hashes are archived and cited.

sections.introduction: Automating intent-to-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises major NetOps productivity gains but creates operational risk when incorrect configurations are enacted. Proposals therefore pair LLMs with automated verifiers and rollback mechanisms to bound risk. We preregistered CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001 to test the primary confirmatory hypothesis H1: that an LLM+verifier (block-on-violation) reduces per-task unsafe-enactment rates relative to LLM-only in a paired design. A preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 concerned verifier-triggered automated rollback reducing service impact. Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and a fully archived deterministic paired run (preregistration SHA256 cited below); (2) an artifact-grounded report of execution, scoring, and validation traces; (3) diagnosis of a deterministic ceiling effect and prescriptive, reproducible next-step designs to reveal verifier utility.
sections.related_work: We situate this experiment within recent LLM-for-NetOps and generate–validate–repair literature, including intent-translation and constrained/validator-assisted LLM pipelines (selected verified works: OpenAlex W7114889968, W7155247165, W7161354925 and Nguyen et al., 2024 doi:10.1002/nem.2313). Prior work emphasizes that operational reliability depends on verifier/tooling and on workflow-centred evaluation rather than standalone model accuracy. Our emphasis is reproducibility: release of per-episode validator traces, scoring JSONs, and deterministic reconciliation to let others replay and stress the same pipelines.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. We preregistered CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001 (SHA256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04). Design: paired confirmatory experiment with 150 confirmatory tasks stratified by intent ambiguity (benign / ambiguous / partially-specified). Generation policy: shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation call per task; at most one repair call). Model: gpt-5-mini (as recorded in execution/model_configuration.json sha256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Verifier/scorer: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; per-episode scoring JSONs record validator fields (required_command_count, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, valid). Execution and logging: adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; all raw outputs, provider-call traces, response files, scoring JSONs, and SHA256 hashes archived (see representative paths and hashes below). Analysis plan: paired McNemar two-sided test (primary), Bonferroni multiplicity control for preregistered confirmatory comparisons, complemented by paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Contamination and exclusions: automatic decontamination rules (non-RFC1918 exclusion, exact-match fingerprinting) were enforced and logged (analysis/contamination_summary.csv).
sections.results: Execution summary (artifact-backed): 150 paired tasks, 300 episodes, model_calls_used = 150 (one initial generation per task) (execution manifest). Baseline valid-configurations = 150/150 (100.0%); Guarded valid-configurations = 150/150 (100.0%). Paired contingency: n11=150, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv sha256 = c2ba9cdb5d0938eae910129ba511eadf309319e6e05b36d9e3b4860032deb80e). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Deterministic reconciliation verifies accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; provider-call audit shows 150 completed hosted-model call events and 0 failures). Representative per-episode artifacts (selected): execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14; execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt sha256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080. Contamination detectors flagged zero contaminated confirmatory tasks (analysis/contamination_summary.csv sha256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222).
sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded diagnosis of the ceiling effect. Two deterministic, archived facts explain the uninformative inferential outcome: (A) identical shared-initial outputs across conditions. For every confirmatory task the baseline and guarded response files are byte-identical (response-file hashes match across conditions; representative files cited above), so the guarded pipeline had no candidate variant to block. (B) validator acceptance predicates were satisfied by every generated candidate: all scoring JSONs show violation_count == 0 and valid == true (representative scoring JSON sha256 above). These facts are recorded in the scoring JSONs and reconciled in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. Consequence: preregistered H2 (rollback success rate and time-to-rollback estimands) was not testable in this execution because no verifier-detected violations occurred and the rollback branch was never invoked. We therefore explicitly correct the preregistration-fidelity metadata: H2 is untested/unexecuted in the confirmatory run (this is artifact-backed; see execution manifest and the absence of rollback events in scoring traces). Practical lessons for future runs (artifact-grounded prescriptions): (1) co-design adversarial/stateful tasks that exercise temporal and cross-command invariants recorded in validator 'pattern' and 'difficulty' fields (e.g., make_before_break_uplink_switchover and paired_link_atomic_mtu_change appear in scoring JSON difficulty.pattern), (2) run multi-model × multi-verifier matrices (e.g., add Batfish-style reachability SMT checks) to surface verifier-dependent discordance, (3) allow independent per-condition generation (not shared_initial) or inject controlled perturbations to produce discordant candidates, and (4) enrich validator predicates to include transient/timing invariants or emulated canary reachability checks rather than purely syntactic acceptance. Reproducibility: all representative artifacts and SHA256 hashes cited above enable immediate verification and replay.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired study of an LLM intent→configuration pipeline with and without an automated verifier. In the executed regime (gpt-5-mini, shared_initial generation, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, 150 paired tasks) all generated candidates satisfied the validator in both pipelines (n11=150), producing a ceiling that made the preregistered inferential tests uninformative (McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap CI [0.0,0.0]). The scientific value is the artifact-backed lesson: benchmark, generator policy, and validator must be co-designed to create discordant outcomes that allow verifier value to be measured. We release the full artifact bundle (preregistration, execution manifest, per-episode scoring JSONs, response files, and analysis scripts with SHA256 hashes) to support adversarial/stateful follow-ups that are likely to reveal verifier-sensitive failure modes.

Generation policy: shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation call per task; at most one repair call), frozen per preregistration. Verifier and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 was the scorer/verifier used; per-episode validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json) record acceptance predicates (required_command_count, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, valid). This deviation is disclosed here and is artifact-backed (no rollback events recorded in scoring JSONs or execution manifest). Human editing: no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock; manuscript revisions responding to peer review were implemented autonomously using the archived artifacts. Limitations: synthetic/emulated benchmark, single-model and single-validator scope, validator acceptance predicates constrain construct validity; these are discussed explicitly in the manuscript's Limitations section.
limitations: Ceiling effect: both pipelines produced validator-acceptable configurations in all 150 confirmatory tasks, preventing the preregistered inferential comparison from being informative.
Synthetic/emulated benchmark: CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1 is synthetic and may not exercise live timing/transient invariants present in production NetOps.
Single-model and single-validator scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; results do not generalize across LLM or verifier families.

Validator predicates: the validator enforced syntactic/semantic predicates recorded in scoring JSONs (e.g., required_command_count, violation_count==0); different verifier designs (reachability SMT, header-space checks) may produce different rejection/rollback behavior.
Rollback hypothesis untested: the preregistered H2 (automated rollback performance) was not testable because the rollback branch was never invoked; this is disclosed and artifact-backed.
Contamination detection limits: automatic detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks, but heuristic scans cannot eliminate subtle training-data leakage.
